summary: Mirage mounts every backend (S3, Slack, Postgres, Datadog, disk, ...) behind one VFS, so a Data Sources explorer is fundamentally a mount tree + per-path file browser, NOT a per-backend native client. The ONLY live browse path that exists today is `GET /api/sessions/{id}/vfs` and `.../vfs/file` (server.py:1876-1900), which literally shell out to `ls -la {path}` and `cat {path}` inside the workspace and string-parse the result (`_parse_ls_output`, server.py:1856). That parse yields only `{name, type:dir|file, size}` — it drops modified-time, fingerprint, revision, mode, and consistency entirely, and file preview is plain decoded text with no binary/truncation handling. The richer console surface (`/api/console/workspaces/{id}/mounts|overlay|effects|trajectory|file`) reads mount metadata (prefix/resource/mode/effect_class) from `ws.mounts()` and op history from `ws.ops.records`, but still never surfaces fingerprint/revision. Crucially, what looks like "Postgres tables", "Datadog dashboards", and "S3 buckets" in the shipped northhill_corp demo are all `FakeXResource(DiskResource)` subclasses (packages/eval/mirage_eval/fixtures/) — a Postgres table is just `tables/<t>/{schema.json,data.jsonl,stats.json}` files on disk, a Datadog source is `logs/<svc>/<date>.jsonl`; so tables+rows+schema and dashboards are browseable/previewable as ordinary files via cat, but there is NO live query engine behind them. The catalog-proxy package (Iceberg/Snowflake/MCP) and the workspace-vfs `query.json`/.schema/.policy/.relationships/.stats layer are fully schema-designed but 100% NotImplementedError stubs — aspirational, not callable. DataBrowser.tsx does not touch the VFS at all; it renders mock REST seed data (/api/tickets, /api/finance/*) as tables and only labels it "Mounted via Arcadia VFS". The real moat — reverse-linking a data path to the traces/steps that touched it — is fully derivable from OpRecord.mount_prefix + OpRecord.path (the records are already collected per command), but the join key (tool_call_id/step_id/run_id) is never stamped onto emitted op events, so attribution is currently inferred by event ordering, not joined.

This is the most solid per-source metadata available.

perTypeNotes:
How each backend TYPE is actually browsed today (grounded in the shipped northhill_corp demo, which mounts Fake*Resource disk doubles, NOT vendor backends):

- s3 / disk (file tree): Native fit. ls -la -> dir/file/size; cat -> bytes. Real S3Resource (resource/s3/s3.py) is_remote=True, SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT=True, fingerprint=ETag, and resolve_glob works — so S3 is the ONE backend that can populate fingerprint/revision for drift/replay. Disk fingerprint = mtime, SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT defaults False. In the demo, /s3 is FakeS3Resource(DiskResource), so even S3 is disk-backed and no ETag flows.

- slack (channels/threads): Browsed as a directory tree of message files (FakeSlackResource = DiskResource). No native channel/thread/message widget; you cat a file to read a thread. A real vendor SlackResource exists but is unused by the demo.

- postgres / iceberg / snowflake (tables+rows+schema): In the demo, /database = FakePostgresResource(DiskResource): each table is tables/<t>/schema.json + data.jsonl + stats.json — so schema (columns/types/PK/FK) and sample rows are READABLE via cat, and that's the whole story. There is NO live SQL. The vendor PostgresResource imports mirage.commands.builtin.postgres + mirage.ops.postgres and registers only filesystem ops (ops/postgres/{read,readdir,stat}.py) — i.e. it presents tables as a filesystem too, not a query API. Iceberg/Snowflake exist ONLY as NotImplementedError catalog-proxy adapter stubs (snowflake has no file at all).

- datadog (dashboards/logs/metrics): NO datadog resource backend exists in vendor/.../resource/ (closest observability backend is langfuse). The demo /datadog = FakeDatadogResource(DiskResource): logs/<svc>/<date>.jsonl + metrics/<svc>/<name>.json. So 'Datadog' is browsed as a log/metric file tree and previewed via cat/jq; there is no dashboards concept and no live query.

- ram (scratch/overlay): The workspace root '/' is RAMResource (WRITE) — agent scratch + write overlay. is_cache==True (source=='ram'), effect_class=scratch.

Net: every source type collapses to 'directory tree + cat preview' today. 'Tables', 'channels', 'dashboards' are naming/layout conventions on top of disk dirs, not type-specific viewers, and nothing is live-queryable.
bridge:
Reverse-linking a data path/mount to the traces & steps that read/wrote it:

WHAT EXISTS: Every observed I/O is an OpRecord (observe/record.py) with op, path (= mount_prefix + rel_path), source, bytes, timestamp, duration_ms, mount_prefix, fingerprint, revision, and is_cache (== source=='ram'). The server already collects per-command op deltas: _execute_in_workspace_detailed (server.py:984) snapshots len(ws.ops.records) before/after each ws.execute() and emits the new records. The console derives three path-keyed views straight off ws.ops.records: _console_trajectory (L2308, full op log with kind read|write|meta + effect_class), _console_effects (L2222, writes only), _console_overlay (L2267, writes grouped per mount). So the cleanest bridge is: filter ws.ops.records (or the persisted trajectory) by mount_prefix==<mount> and/or path startswith <path>. The relay 'op' StreamEvent (L1006-1018) and the AG-UI 'vfs_op' CUSTOM event (L1401-1412) also carry path + mount_prefix, so a path can be matched against the firehose too.

THE JOIN-KEY GAP (this is the one real blocker, matching the reframe Phase-0 note): op events are NOT stamped with tool_call_id/step_id/run_id. In the streaming turn (L1383-1412) new_ops are produced INSIDE the `for cmd` loop where tc_id is in scope, but the emitted vfs_op value is only {op,path,bytes,mount_prefix} — tc_id is dropped on the floor. The relay 'op' event drops it too and additionally drops fingerprint/revision (it forwards op/path/source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix only; OpRecord.fingerprint/revision/is_cache never leave the process). Attribution is done by length-diffing ws.ops.records, not by consuming ExecutionNode.records. Consequence: path->step/run links must be reconstructed by EVENT ORDERING (the ops emitted between a TOOL_CALL_START and the next one belong to that exec) and must be labeled INFERRED until tool_call_id (+ source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision) are stamped at emission. Path->command/op is solid; path->step/run is inferred.

The workspace-vfs metadata.py also defines a RelationshipEntry (.relationships) model for cross-SOURCE joins (source_a.column_a <-> source_b.column_b), which would let the explorer bridge data-to-data, but it is an unimplemented stub.
gotchas: VFS browse is string-parsed `ls -la`/`cat` (server.py:1856 _parse_ls_output, 1884/1898). It captures ONLY name/type/size — modified-time, fingerprint, revision, mode, consistency are all parsed away even though FileStat/OpRecord carry them. Preview/diff fidelity is text-only: no binary detection, no truncation marker, no byte range — large/binary files will be mangled and must be labeled 'preview only'.

DataBrowser.tsx is NOT a data-source explorer. It calls /api/tickets, /api/finance/*, /api/customers/* etc. (mock REST seed data) and renders tables, while labeling them 'Mounted via Arcadia VFS'. It never calls vfsList/vfsFile or catalog-proxy. The only real VFS browser is VFSExplorer.tsx.

catalog-proxy is 100% NotImplementedError: CatalogProxy.resolve/execute_query, and every IcebergAdapter/McpAdapter/BaseAdapter method. SourceRegistry.list_sources works but only returns [{id,type}]. There is NO Snowflake or Postgres adapter file — only iceberg.py, mcp.py, base.py. Treat all 'queryable catalog' capability as aspirational.

workspace-vfs is also stub-level: WorkspaceTree.readdir/getattr raise NotImplementedError. Its value today is the SCHEMA contract — QuerySpec (sql|glob|similarity|search), and the .schema/.policy/.relationships/.stats/.manifest Pydantic models — not runnable behavior.

The shipped demo's 'Postgres', 'Datadog', 'S3', 'Slack' are Fake*Resource(DiskResource) doubles in packages/eval/mirage_eval/fixtures/. So 'tables/rows/schema' and 'logs/metrics' are just JSON files on disk; there is no live query, no live ETag/revision, and no real backend connection. An explorer built on the demo will show disk dirs dressed up as exotic sources.

No datadog resource backend exists in vendor/.../resource/ at all (the observability backend that ships is langfuse). 'Datadog dashboards' is purely the fake disk layout (logs/*.jsonl + metrics/*.json).

fingerprint/revision flow only for backends with SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT=True. Only S3Resource sets it True (ETag). disk/ram/the fakes default False, so for the demo, fingerprint is at best disk mtime (DiskResource.fingerprint) and revision is None — drift/version UI cannot be populated from the demo data.

Cache state surfaces only as a derived signal: OpRecord.is_cache == (source=='ram'). A genuine cache hit emits no separate OpRecord, so 'served from cache' must be derived (is_cache / absence of a network op), per the reframe. Don't present it as a first-class recorded event.

The op-event firehose is a 2000-entry RAM ring (per reframe) and the console caches overlay/effects/trajectory in-memory on the ConsoleWorkspace; a dev console watching ALL workspace ops must paginate/persist via arcadia_store, not rely on these.

summary: Today there is NOT one unified action stream — there are TWO parallel streams with two different ordering keys. (1) The relay firehose: `server.py` `_emit_event`/`_console_emit` → `_persist_and_broadcast`, which stamps a global monotonic `seq` (`_next_stream_seq`) + `timestamp`, appends to a 5000-deque + `stream_events` table, and fans out on the `/events` SSE consumed by `useEventStream`. It only carries `command`, `op`, `agent_status`, `agent_thinking`, and `console_*` events. (2) The AG-UI run stream: `_run_conversation_turn_stream` yields RUN/STEP/THINKING/TEXT/TOOL_CALL_*/CUSTOM(vfs_op) events that go ONLY to the per-session SSE (`/api/sessions/{id}/message/stream`), are reduced by `aguiEventReducer.ts` into `sessionRunStore`, and are coalesced+persisted to `agui_events` with a per-SESSION `seq` via `StreamCoalescer`. These AG-UI events never hit `_persist_and_broadcast`, so they carry NO global `seq` — only a millisecond `timestamp`. So the "everything in the workspace" stream the reframe wants does not exist yet; it must be assembled client-side by merging the global firehose (seq-ordered) with per-session agui_events (per-session-seq-ordered) on `timestamp`, which is lossy at sub-ms granularity. Time-travel state reconstruction is PARTIAL: the per-op trajectory, RAM-overlay write set, reads-so-far, and pending effects are all derivable op-by-op from `ws.ops.records` (the OpRecord ground-truth leaf) and the existing `_console_overlay`/`_console_trajectory`/`_console_effects` endpoints; but full-FS state at action N is NOT reconstructable because written-mount backing is pinned only at stand-up (one `ws.snapshot()` tar) and cache hits emit no OpRecord. STATE_SNAPSHOT/STATE_DELTA exist as enum names ONLY — never emitted, reduced, coalesced, or stored. The closest existing UI is the console `StatePage` (overlay diff + backing/effective browser), `TrajectoryPage` (filterable op log + JSON export), and `RunPage` (live run trace) — none has a time-travel cursor, per-action diff, jump-to/skip, or future-dimming.

perTypeNotes:
HOW EACH EVENT TYPE FLOWS + ITS ORDERING KEY / CORRELATION IDS:

RELAY FIREHOSE (global `seq`, ms `timestamp`; carries `agent`,`session`/`session_id`):
- `command{command,exit_code,stdout,cwd?,agent,session}` — one per shell exec, emitted in _execute_in_workspace_detailed.
- `op{op,path,source,bytes,duration_ms,mount_prefix,agent,session}` — emitted from ws.ops.records DELTA (length-diff `all_records[ops_before:]`, capped at last 20). NOTE: fingerprint/revision/is_cache are DROPPED here even though OpRecord carries them.
- `agent_status{status,task?,error?}`, `agent_thinking{message}` — coarse lifecycle.
- `console_standup|console_branch|console_promote|console_mode|console_reset|console_test_run{workspace_id,…}` — workspace lifecycle; the ONLY events that carry `workspace_id`. ConsoleLayout refreshes the active workspace when one arrives.
- `mock_request{service,method,path,status_code,response_bytes,duration_ms}` and `mcp_tool_call{tool,arguments,result,result_bytes,duration_ms,error}` — documented (eval/AGENTS.md) and produced by packages/eval/mirage_eval/mcp_server.py; they only enter the platform via POST /ingest, NOT from the in-process agent.

AG-UI RUN STREAM (per-session SSE only; per-SESSION `seq` assigned at persistence by StreamCoalescer; ms `timestamp`; NO global seq):
- RUN_STARTED/RUN_FINISHED/RUN_ERROR{thread_id=session.id, run_id} — run-{uuid} is the trace root.
- STEP_STARTED/STEP_FINISHED{step_id, step_name} — step-N; reducer attaches to currentRunId.
- THINKING_START/CONTENT/END{thinking_id, step_id?}; TEXT_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END{message_id, role}.
- TOOL_CALL_START{tool_call_id, tool_name='exec'}/ARGS{delta=raw shell}/RESULT{result,exit_code}/END — one TOOL_CALL == one ws.execute().
- CUSTOM{name='vfs_op', value:{op,path,bytes,mount_prefix}} — the data-plane leaf, but value is TRIMMED to 4 fields (source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision/is_cache dropped) and carries NO tool_call_id.

INTERLEAVING REALITY: the reframe's premise that AG-UI + relay StreamEvents + VfsOps + mock_requests already interleave in one seq-ordered firehose is FALSE today. AG-UI events and relay `op`/`command` events are emitted from the SAME code path (_execute_in_workspace_detailed emits relay op/command via _emit_event; the surrounding _run_conversation_turn_stream yields the AG-UI TOOL_CALL/CUSTOM) but land on DIFFERENT transports with DIFFERENT counters. To build the unified log you must merge: (a) /events firehose by global seq, (b) per-session agui_events (GET /api/sessions/{id}/trace, ordered by its own seq), joining on `session`/`thread_id` and `timestamp`. There is no single monotonic key spanning both.

CLIENT-SIDE CORRELATION: correlateEvents.ts buckets firehose StreamEvents into steps purely by TIMESTAMP windows (started_at..ended_at) and filters by `session` — it is the existing, explicitly-`inferred` op→step attribution; it does NOT use run_id/step_id/tool_call_id (those aren't on relay op events).
bridge:
MAPPING ONTO REDUX DEVTOOLS:

- ACTION LIST ← the merged stream. Best stable index = relay `seq` for firehose events; per-session `agui_events.seq` for run events. Each row's 'action type' = event `.type`; payload = the event dict. The op-indexed trajectory (`idx` == position in ws.ops.records) is a parallel, gap-free action index specifically for data-plane ops and is the cleanest cursor for state reconstruction.

- STATE TREE INSPECTOR ← reconstructed workspace state. Buildable NOW by folding trajectory entries[0..N]: effective VFS overlay (per-mount write set from _console_overlay, change key idx:op:path), mounts (prefix/resource/mode/effect_class from _console_mounts_detail), reads-so-far set (read ops up to N), pending effects (writes not in promoted_keys), last-known per-path bytes. RunStep/ToolCall maps from the reducer give the reasoning/tool sub-tree.

- PER-ACTION STATE DIFF ← diff(stateAt(N-1), stateAt(N)). For data-plane this is exact and trivial: action N is exactly OpRecord[N], so the diff is that single op (path, +bytes, op kind) — already what OverlayDiff renders per change. For run-level, diff successive reducer snapshots (new message delta, new tool call, new step). No diff engine exists yet; it must be added but the inputs are present.

- JUMP-TO / SKIP-ACTION ← recompute stateAt(N) by re-folding entries[0..N] (jump) or entries[0..N] minus the skipped idx (skip). Pure client-side over the trajectory array; the existing replayAguiEvents() already proves deterministic fold-from-empty for the run sub-tree.

- FUTURE-DIMMING ← trivial: dim every action with index > cursor in the action list.

- IMPORT / EXPORT ← export EXISTS (TrajectoryPage exportJson dumps entries). Import/replay does not; the raw material for true replay is the agui_events trace (GET /api/sessions/{id}/trace → replayAguiEvents) plus the pinned snapshot tar (Workspace.load via build_mount_args/apply_state_dict).

HONEST LIMITS THE BRIDGE MUST RESPECT:
1. RECONSTRUCTABLE at action N: VFS write-overlay, mounts, reads-so-far, pending/captured effects, run/step/reasoning/tool sub-tree, last STATE_SNAPSHOT (none today) — all op-by-op derivable.
2. NOT RECONSTRUCTABLE: byte-exact full filesystem of WRITTEN mounts before/at N (backing is pinned ONCE at stand-up as a single tar; there is no per-tick snapshot). StatePage already labels the Backing layer 'Pinned at stand-up … pre-overlay reconstruction … deferred'. Cache-hit reads emit NO OpRecord (OpRecord.is_cache==source=='ram'), so 'served from cache' is DERIVED, not an action — the action list will have gaps vs. true I/O.
3. The two-counter problem: jump-to across the *combined* AG-UI+relay log can only order by timestamp; same-ms events have undefined relative order. A true single seq requires Phase-0 plumbing (route AG-UI events through _persist_and_broadcast too, stamp run_id/step_id/tool_call_id on relay op events, and fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer).
gotchas: TWO STREAMS, TWO COUNTERS: AG-UI run events (RUN/STEP/THINKING/TEXT/TOOL_CALL/CUSTOM) NEVER pass through _persist_and_broadcast, so they have NO global seq — only ms timestamp. The /events firehose (useEventStream) and the per-session AG-UI stream (useAgentStream/sessionRunStore) are independent transports; the reframe's 'unified seq-ordered firehose of everything' does not exist yet.

STATE_SNAPSHOT / STATE_DELTA are dead enum names only (types/agui.ts L17-18). Never emitted, never in the aguiEventReducer switch, never coalesced, never stored. Do not present Redux-style state events as real.

VfsOp emission is doubly lossy: (a) relay `op` events and the AG-UI CUSTOM(vfs_op) value both DROP fingerprint/revision/is_cache (OpRecord HAS them); the CUSTOM value keeps only op/path/bytes/mount_prefix. (b) The coalescer writes VfsOpRow with run_id but NEVER sets tool_call_id (defaults None) even though the column exists — exactly the reframe Phase-0 gap. op→tool_call attribution is currently impossible from stored rows.

Relay `op` events are computed by length-diffing ws.ops.records (all_records[ops_before:]) and CAPPED at the last 20 ops per command (server.py L1006) — high-fan-out commands silently lose ops from the firehose. The AG-UI CUSTOM path (new_ops) is uncapped, so the two streams can disagree on op count.

correlateEvents.ts attributes firehose events to steps purely by TIMESTAMP windows and a session filter — it does NOT use run_id/step_id/tool_call_id. This is the explicitly-'inferred' correlation; overlapping/zero-duration steps mis-bucket.

Derived tables runs/steps/tool_calls/vfs_ops are WRITE-ONLY today: sql_store exposes get_trace (raw agui_events payloads) but NO read method for vfs_ops/runs/steps/tool_calls. Time-travel that wants the persisted op log must add queries or recompute from the live workspace (/trajectory endpoint, which needs a live ws — lost after restart unless re-stood-up).

Backing/full-FS time travel is impossible per-action: a single snapshot tar is pinned at stand-up (console_standup), not per tick. Written-mount pre-state cannot be byte-reconstructed; StatePage and TrajectoryPage both already carry 'deferred' labels for this.
Cache hits emit no OpRecord (is_cache == source=='ram'), so the action stream has gaps vs. real I/O; 'served from cache' must be rendered as derived, never as a missing/failed read.

mock_request and mcp_tool_call are produced only by packages/eval/mirage_eval/mcp_server.py and reach the platform solely via POST /ingest — the in-process console agent never emits them, so a workspace-scoped console will usually show zero unless an external eval agent is feeding /ingest.

The console firehose is GLOBAL, not workspace-scoped: ConsoleLayout calls useEventStream('/events') with no workspace/session filter; only console_* events carry workspace_id. Scoping 'all events in THIS workspace' requires client-side filtering by session-of-workspace, but relay op/command events use the agent session id, not the console workspace id.

Persistence degrades silently to in-memory (_setup_persistence) — when off, agui_events/stream_events are not durable, so trace replay and any time-travel-after-restart return empty; the UI must distinguish 'clean' from 'not persisted'.

Two ordering subtleties in the firehose: stream_events seq is assigned in _persist_and_broadcast and is process-global (survives restart via max_stream_seq), but agui_events seq is per-session (next_seq = max+1 per session_id). Never assume one global index across both tables.
